name: Theerthapureeswarar Temple, Tiruvathurai
deity: Shiva as Theerthapureeswarar (Arathurainathar), with the goddess Anandanayaki
period: Ancient Shaiva shrine of the Nadu Nadu country, sung in the Tevaram (7th century); medieval Chola-period sculpture and later additions
summary: Theerthapureeswarar is the Tirunelvayil Aratturai of the Tevaram hymns, counted the first of the Nadu Nadu shrines praised by the saints, and remembered above all as the place where the child saint Sambandar was gifted a pearl palanquin, a pearl umbrella and pearl insignia.

sections.history: Tiruvathurai lies in the Nadu Nadu country of present-day Cuddalore district and appears in the Tevaram hymns as Tirunelvayil Aratturai. Tradition counts it the first of the Nadu Nadu shrines praised by the saints, which makes it a Paadal Petra Sthalam. The lord is worshipped as Aratturainathar, Anandeeswarar and Theerthapureeswarar, and the goddess as Anandanayaki, a name that sources also give as Tirupurasundari. The temple is linked with the Tevaram saints Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, and its fame rests above all on the gift of the pearl palanquin to the child saint Sambandar, a scene told in the Periya Puranam and shown in the Chola-period stucco and sculpture of the temple. The shrine has been kept in worship through the medieval centuries and after.
sections.architecture: Sources describe the towers and halls of Tiruvathurai only thinly, so this account keeps to what is recorded. The temple is a Tamil Shaiva shrine with a sanctum for the lord and a shrine for the goddess Anandanayaki. What sets it apart is its sculpture: the story of the pearl palanquin is carried in Chola-period stucco and stone, and one depiction, said to be the earliest known, shows the palanquin approaching the saint and his father. Visitors who come for the art should look for these figures within the temple.
sections.legends: The legend of Tiruvathurai belongs to the child Sambandar. After receiving the milk of knowledge at Sirkazhi, he set out to visit the shrines of Shiva, usually carried on his father's shoulders. On the way to Tirunelvayil he refused to be carried and walked, and his companions were grieved to see the boy go barefoot over the hot ground. That night, the story says, Arathurainathar appeared in the dreams of the temple servants and of the saint himself, and promised a pearl palanquin, a pearl umbrella and pearl insignia to spare the child his hardship. By morning the gifts lay in the temple, and Sambandar accepted them as the Lord's grace. Tradition keeps from this a Lord who answers a child's weariness with tenderness.
sections.festivals: The festivals recorded for the temple are Maha Shivaratri in February or March, Margazhi Tiruvadhirai in December or January, and Panguni Uthiram in March or April. The monthly Pradosham is observed as at every Shiva temple. The calendar of local observances is thinly documented, so confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Tiruvathurai is a village shrine, and it asks to be approached unhurriedly, much as the child saint is said to have come to it, on foot and without ceremony. Pause among the Chola-period figures that tell the story of the pearl palanquin, then come to the sanctum of Aratturainathar and to the goddess Anandanayaki in her own shrine. The setting is quiet farming country, and the temple keeps the stillness of a very old place of worship where an old tale is still part of daily memory.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvathurai is a village in Tittagudi taluk of Cuddalore district (PIN 606111), a short distance from Pennadam, which has its own railway station. Virudhachalam and Tittagudi are the larger towns of the area. Plan the journey by train or bus to Pennadam or Virudhachalam and complete the last stretch by road; confirm local transport on the day.
